subject: Contract remedies: holdback / termination escalation request
messages:
From: Emma Hayes <emma.hayes@aceta.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@aceta.com, contracts@aceta.com
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 08:15:00 -0400
Subject: Contract remedies & termination rights (SLA)

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the time on the call yesterday. Aceta’s procurement and legal teams have reviewed the draft SLA and we have one material concern that prevents us from moving forward on the proposed commercial terms: the current remedies are limited to service credits only. For our regulated workflows (patient-facing inference at scale) we need stronger economic and exit protections.

Specifically we are asking Redwood to:
- Place a fee holdback equal to 15% of the annual committed spend into an escrow arrangement during year one (to be released subject to performance milestones).
- Provide an unconditional termination right for Aceta if a single regional outage exceeds 4 consecutive hours of total unavailability for our production cluster.
- Agree to liquidated damages for severity-1 incidents that exceed the monthly credit cap (to be defined in the redline).

We understand this is beyond Redwood’s standard posture. Please treat the attached redline as Aceta’s starting point and let us have a written counterproposal by Friday, 29 May. Our procurement timeline is tight — we plan to commit to a vendor by mid-June.

Also flag: Aceta operates an EU data residency requirement; any proposed remedy needs to be compatible with our local compliance team.

Thanks,
Emma Hayes
Director, Strategic Sourcing
Aceta Health

Attachment: aceta_redline_v1.docx (redline of Redwood agreement)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Emma Hayes <emma.hayes@aceta.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contract remedies & termination rights (SLA)

Emma — thanks for the clear note and the redline. I appreciate Aceta’s urgency and the context on regulated workloads. I’ve looped in Marcus (sales lead) and Laura (legal) so we can coordinate.

Initial thoughts:
- We absolutely want you to feel protected. However, a 15% holdback into escrow is materially outside our standard enterprise posture and would create an operational impedance for capacity planning.
- We can consider a mitigated alternative that balances both sides: a modest holdback (to be escrowed) plus an objective incident definition and a staged termination path after repeat severe breaches.

Can Marcus and the infra team confirm whether the 4-hr unconditional termination trigger can be technical scoped (e.g., must be verified across monitoring signals, affect >50% of your routed traffic, and after an attempted mitigation window)? Laura — can your team prepare a redline alternative that preserves termination as a backstop but with a cure/verification process?

If you’re available, I’d propose a short call this week to walk the alternatives and agree an interim counterproposal that we can both take to counsel.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Emma Hayes <emma.hayes@aceta.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contract remedies & termination rights (SLA)

Emma / team — quick technical context from infra and a proposed commercial counter (attached).

Technical notes:
- Redwood’s production routing provides per-region failover; a 4-hour outage in one AZ typically would be mitigated by cross-region routing unless the incident is global.
- For multi-tenant hosted customers, sustained unavailability at the per-customer level is rare; worst-case is a regional incident that can be resolved with an emergency capacity shift.

Commercial counterproposal (high level):
- Holdback: 5% of year-one committed fees placed in escrow, released quarterly based on meeting availability milestones (we can define milestones tied to regional uptime and response-time SLOs).
- Termination: Allow termination for cause only after two separate qualifying severity-1 incidents impacting Aceta (each incident >3 hours of verified unavailability), or one incident plus failure to cure within a 30-day remediation window; not an automatic termination on a single 4-hour incident.
- Liquidated damages: capped at 25% of the quarter’s fees; otherwise, service credits scale by severity with clear measurement definitions.

Attachments: SLA_technical_notes.pdf, proposed_counter_v1.docx

We think this gives Aceta stronger economic protection while keeping an operationally feasible path for Redwood. Happy to jump on the call and work through the definitions for a final legal redline.

—Marcus
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Emma Hayes <emma.hayes@aceta.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@aceta.com, contracts@aceta.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 14:10:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Contract remedies & termination rights (SLA)

Thanks Marcus — helpful context. A few points from Aceta legal that are non-negotiable for our Board and compliance reviews:
- We need an ability to terminate after a single verified production-impacting outage >4 hours for our primary EU cluster. Our environment cannot tolerate a prolonged unavailability even if it is regionally contained.
- If Redwood insists on a multi-incident trigger, the holdback needs to be at least 12% of the committed spend and should be held in an independent escrow (not Redwood-controlled).

We’re willing to narrow definitions (verification signals, traffic impact thresholds) but not to remove the single-incident termination right for our primary EU production cluster.

Our timeline is firm — we require a written answer on whether Redwood can accommodate an independent escrow and single-incident termination for the EU cluster by Tuesday, 1 June. If we can’t reach agreement, we will have to continue evaluating alternatives.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/prepare/abc123-contract-redline (Aceta redline attached there)

—Emma
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Emma Hayes <emma.hayes@aceta.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 16:42:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Contract remedies & termination rights (SLA)

Emma — thank you for the candor and the timeline. We want to reach a commercial solution that supports Aceta’s regulatory needs while keeping a workable operational model. Proposed compromise below:

1) Holdback / escrow: Redwood will agree to an independent escrow equal to 7.5% of year-one committed fees. Funds will be released quarterly against predefined availability milestones (we’ll propose metrics and objective measurement tools in the SLA appendix).

2) Termination carve for EU production: We will permit termination for cause after a single verified production-impacting outage >4 hours for Aceta’s primary EU cluster, but only if all of the following are met:
   - The incident is validated by mutually agreed monitoring signals and an independent third-party (technical auditor) if requested;
   - Redwood has attempted mitigation and executed a documented incident response within the incident window;
   - The customer provides notice of intent to terminate within 30 days of the incident and both parties engage in a post-incident review — termination is the backstop if remediation is not feasible.

3) Liquidated damages / cap: For qualifying S1 incidents we will accept a liquidated damages framework limited to a hard cap of 3 months of recurring fees in year one. Outside of that cap, credits will continue to apply.

4) Additional safeguards: We’ll offer a quarterly SLA review with Aceta’s site reliability leads for the first year and an operational playbook for failover and runbooks to reduce recurrence risk.

If this is acceptable, we’ll produce a focused redline for the EU cluster appendix and set a 45-minute call with our legal and infra teams tomorrow (please propose a time). If not, we need to know what components are still blocking you.

—Vivek
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_compromise_counter.docx
